$schema_note: Forge Lexicon v1.0.3 — canonical mapping from internal (lineage) vocabulary to public-surface vocabulary. Consumed by: translation passes, term-leak linter, lineage document. This file is itself a public artifact; it contains no secrets, only naming policy.

brand.policy: The public brand is 'Solomon's Forge', admitted as a scoped exception via brand_allowlist below. The brand is a label, never technical vocabulary: specifications refer to 'the Forge handoff contract', 'Forge core invariants'. The name 'Solomon's Key' is reserved for the future public release of the protocol manifest language and is recorded as reserved in LINEAGE.md.
brand.rationale: Evocative brands on rigorously plain engineering are industry-normal (Prometheus, Kafka, Kubernetes). The brand exception is mechanically scoped: the exact string is permitted only in designated files; all other occurrences of the pattern remain violations.

brand_allowlist.rule: In allowed_files only, each exact occurrence of an allowed string is removed from a line before pattern matching. All other matches, in any file, remain violations. The allowlist never applies to spec/**, src/**, examples/**, or test/**.

scopes.public_surface: Everything in the repository except excluded_paths: README, specifications, code identifiers, examples, tests, CI config, package metadata, published docs
scopes.internal_only: Lineage document, private build notes, pass reports on the private side, conversation shorthand

entries.public_term: Solomon's Forge (brand, allowlisted files only) / Forge (in technical prose)
entries.notes: Pattern still catches any 'Solomon' variant; the brand_allowlist carves the sole exception. Bare 'Solomon' is a violation everywhere, including allowlisted files.

entries.public_term: Forge protocol specification (current); name reserved for future protocol manifest language release
entries.notes: Covered by the Solomon pattern above; NOT in the allowlist. The reservation is documented in LINEAGE.md.

Industry-standard term for a declarative file a runtime validates and executes. File naming convention on public surface: *.manifest.yaml. Bare word 'key' is NOT linted (too common); only the compound forms are.
Describes function rather than asserting it. 'Runtime' alone is acceptable where context is unambiguous.
HIGHEST-PRIORITY translation; most lore-dependent term. Long form where precision matters: 'deterministic tool contract'. Code identifiers: sealedTool / SealedTool.
Covered by Hollow patterns above. 'Local execution shim' or 'simulated service layer' are both acceptable.

entries.notes: Public phrasing: 'the log attests'.
Public phrasing: 'tests validate'. Narrow pattern to avoid false positives.

entries.notes: The orchestration system remains private in v1. Revisit when/if the runtime is published.

linter_policy.match_mode: regex, word-boundary, case-sensitive as written per pattern
linter_policy.on_hit: fail CI with file, line, matched pattern, and suggested public term
linter_policy.policy_note: v1.0.3 inverts coverage: everything is scanned except narrow exclusions. This closes the recurring class of gap where new directories (.github, test, examples) were silently unscanned. v1.0.4 excludes docs/case-study-gates.md: an incident record that quotes rule violations verbatim as evidence, per the same rationale as LINEAGE.md.
linter_policy.known_false_positive_guidance: The words 'key', 'judge', 'pass', 'gate' in ordinary English are permitted; only the compound/branded patterns listed above are violations.

lineage_policy.purpose: Records the original vocabulary, the mapping in this file, why the names existed, and the reservation of 'Solomon's Key' for the future protocol manifest language release.
lineage_policy.rule: Lineage is culture, not interface. It never leads public documents and is never required reading to evaluate the framework.
